chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, from his brother Ali, from al-Husayn, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Ibn Sinan, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):
regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'Then let them end their tafath'
He said: It is shaving and what is in the skin of a person.

key_terms.تَفَث: Ritual shaving and removal of impurities from the body

ai.seo_question: What does the term 'tafath' mean in the context of Islamic ritual purity and Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the term 'tafath' in Surah al-Hajj as the removal of bodily impurities, specifically hair and dirt from the skin, linking it to the ritual purification of the body. This exegetical insight underscores the Shia emphasis on physical cleanliness as an integral component of spiritual devotion during the Hajj rites. The definition highlights the tangible aspect of 'purging impurities' before completing the pilgrimage.
